# Admin Google accounts (comma-separated emails). These users get is_admin on sign-in.
PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS=you@gmail.com
# Local only: skip Google sign-in and auto-login as the first PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS
# address. Honored only on 127.0.0.1 / localhost — never on kuchup.com.
# PANEL_AUTH_DISABLED=1
# Legacy username still used by the fetch scheduler when resolving an admin user id
PANEL_ADMIN_USER=admin

def test_auth_disabled_auto_logins_admin_on_localhost(client, db, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PANEL_AUTH_DISABLED", "1")
    monkeypatch.setenv("PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS", "admin@example.com")
    body = client.get("/api/auth/status").get_json()
    assert body["authenticated"] is True
    assert body["user"]["email"] == "admin@example.com"
    assert body["user"]["is_admin"] is True


def test_auth_disabled_ignored_off_localhost(client, db, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("PANEL_AUTH_DISABLED", "1")
    body = client.get("/api/auth/status", headers={"Host": "kuchup.com"}).get_json()
    assert body["authenticated"] is False

Local login is off. Open [http://127.0.0.1:5051/panel](http://127.0.0.1:5051/panel) — you are auto-signed in as admin, no Google prompt.

`PANEL_AUTH_DISABLED=1` is set in your local `.env`, using the existing `PANEL_ADMIN_EMAILS` account. That flag is ignored on anything other than `127.0.0.1` / `localhost`, so kuchup.com is unchanged.

Restarted the panel on 5051 so this is live. To turn Google sign-in back on locally, set `PANEL_AUTH_DISABLED=0` and restart.
